title: Resting-state fMRI classifier separates minimally conscious from unresponsive wakefulness
summary: In 94 patients from two centers (discovery n=48, external validation n=46), L1-regularized logistic regression selected 10 core fMRI features dominated by default-mode, cerebellar and subcortical coupling. The best classifier, an SVM, reached an AUC of 0.859, accuracy of 82.6% and sensitivity of 90.5% in the external cohort. SHAP circuit interpretation is correlational, and the cohorts are very small; this is a version 1 preprint.
ai_technology: L1-regularized logistic regression feature selection, nine optimized classifiers (best SVM) and SHAP on regional and network rs-fMRI markers

evidence.tested: External validation cohort from an independent center (n=46).
evidence.unknown: Larger-cohort performance, causal role of the networks and clinical use; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Classifies disorder-of-consciousness diagnosis from fMRI markers and ranks contributing circuits.
